extracted.intended_audience: aspiring comedians and performers (adults, teens) looking for Second City-style training in Chicago
extracted.subtask_description: Listings and learning-objectives for Second City Training Center classes (improv, sketch writing, stand-up, acting, open-stage formats) intended to help students develop comedic skills and find their voice. Includes beginner-through-advanced class descriptions and suitability indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental principle: “Yes, And”
rubrics_metrics.description: Improv 1 introduces students to the fundamental concept of “Yes, And” in improvisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Through group exercises and games, students will explore impulse & spontaneity, listening, being present in the ... (course framed around learning and applying the ‘Yes, And’ principle).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impulse & spontaneity
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will explore impulse & spontaneity as a core improv skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developed through group exercises and games in beginner improv courses (presented as skills to cultivate for successful improvisation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Listening
rubrics_metrics.description: Active listening is taught as a key component of improvisational work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasized in group exercises and games to support scene work and responsiveness onstage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Being present
rubrics_metrics.description: Being present in the moment is a stated objective for improv students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taught via experiential exercises to improve spontaneity, listening, and scene work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenic comedy writing (foundation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing 1 is described as the foundation for scenic comedy writing and for writing to/for a Second City-style revue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A guide for utilizing improvised material and techniques to create written scenes suitable for revue performance (course framed as the beginning of scenic comedy craft).

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Stages as testing ground
rubrics_metrics.description: Open Stages provides an experimental space for current students to try out new ideas and material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students can use this time to test stand-up, storytelling, sketch, music, or improv—intended for trying and refining material in front of a live audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining improvisation with scripted media (acting)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Second City Acting Program combines improvisational techniques with a variety of scripted media—including materials from the Second City archive—to build foundations of grounded acting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course uses improv methods plus scripted texts (archive material) to develop grounded, scene-based acting skills for comedic performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solo comedic performance: writing & workshopping material
rubrics_metrics.description: Stand-Up 1 focuses on developing the student as a solo comedic performer by writing and workshopping their own material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students will write, workshop, and perform stand-up pieces; the class frames iterative writing-and-feedback as central to building a stand-up act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study of stand-up tradition/history to inform practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Stand-Up 1 includes understanding how earlier stand-up comics evolved as part of the pedagogy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students learn from the development/evolution of prior comedians to inform experimentation and growth in their own material and stage persona.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introductory flexible format (Improv 1A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Improv 1A offers a fun and flexible way to dive into the basics of improvisation in a shorter (4-week) format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed for students not ready to commit to a full term—provides condensed exposure to foundational improv skills and concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class-fit / suitability indicators (Good for:)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each class lists intended use-cases or ‘Good for’ categories (e.g., Improv, Writing, Student Events, Acting, Stand Up).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tags guide prospective students about which class aligns with their goals (e.g., Writing 1 -> writing; Open Stages -> student events/testing material).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding your voice in comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Training Center promises help in finding your voice in comedy as an overall program objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as an outcome of taking the right classes and progressing through study—promoted via a quiz and class pathways to match students to appropriate courses.
